text:
maya: Heads-up — over the last 3 hours we're seeing sustained tail-latency spikes on eu-west dedicated slices. latency SLA breaches correlate with lots of long-streaming hosted requests + a surge in small-chat embedding churn.

raj: Seen it. Telemetry looks like proxy-level connection ejections + repeated KV-cache invalidations. Dedicated slice CPU is fine but GPU runqueue jumps.

luca: Are we sure it's not just a model change? any recent rollout?

maya: No model rollout that matches the timing. deploy-bot: deploys/hosted: no deploys to generation-serving in last 6h. infra-bot: rolling telemetry snapshot attached -> proxy_eject_rate up 4.3x, kvcache_eviction_rate up 6x, per-token latency p99 from 320ms -> 780ms.

tasha: This pattern smells like long-lived streams keeping KV cache shards pinned while many tiny embedding jobs thrash the cache. Shared eviction causing extra host memory pressure and proxy to start ejecting based on active_conn heuristics.

raj: If proxy is ejecting TCPs, requests fall back to other pools -> added cold starts and queueing. Need to stop the initial ejection loop. Can we add a fast backpressure gate at the proxy to shed or enqueue non-SLO-critical streams?

maya: Proposal: 1) Add a short-term opt-in backpressure rule in the proxy that'll rate-limit streaming connections per-tenant when kvcache_eviction_rate > threshold. 2) Add a scheduler signal from proxy -> scheduler (egress_backpressure) so scheduler avoids spilling dedicated slices for those tenants. 3) Tune dedicated pool min-reserve to avoid immediate preemptions until the backpressure gate stabilizes.

luca: Sounds good. How invasive is (1)? can we do a header check + token bucket in front proxy config?

raj: Minimal. Example nginx-ish snippet we can toggle via flag: 

```
# proxy rate-limit pseudo-config
limit_req_zone $tenant_token zone=tenantburst:10m rate=10r/s;
server {
  location /stream {
    if ($kvcache_eviction_rate > 1000) {
      limit_req zone=tenantburst burst=20 nodelay;
    }
  }
}
```

tasha: We need TTL-safe defaults — don't want to throttle legitimate low-volume streaming apps. Suggest adding whitelist for Dedicated customers with SLO=high.

oncall: Current incident page updated: https://incidents/redwood/174345. We're seeing 12% dedicated-slice spillover to shared in eu-west, and 22% higher token cost due to retries. Root cause correlates to mix of long streaming sessions + small embedding fanout.

maya: I propose immediate 30-minute mitigation window: enable proxy backpressure (gradually, 10% of proxy fleet -> 50% -> 100%), increase dedicated pool min-reserve by 1.5x, and pause any auto-slicing shrink policies. Can we get owners for each step?

raj: I'll own the proxy rollout. Will implement a feature flag and a canary at 10% immediately.

luca: I'll handle scheduler signal and a short-term hold on spillover-trigger logic. I'll create a toggle in the scheduler control plane to ignore proxy-spill heuristics for 30m windows.

tasha: I'll update the Dedicated sizing template and flip min-reserve in eu-west to +50% for the next 1h. Also add tenants with high SLO to the whitelist.

infra-bot: telemetry-check: scheduled auto-checks will run at +5m, +15m, +30m after each change. Alert if p99 not below 500ms or kvcache_eviction_rate not reduced by 40%.

oncall: Also add cost-watch — retries are burning tokens. Finance wants a quick estimate of delta if this continues for another 6 hours.

maya: Action items:
- raj: implement proxy backpressure flag + canary (ETA 15m)
- luca: scheduler hold toggle + short-circuit signal (ETA 20m)
- tasha: resize min-reserve + whitelist flip (ETA 10m)
- oncall: coordinate incident page + cost estimate (ETA 25m)

raj: starting canary now. will post logs and curl commands. :eyes: 

luca: hooked scheduler to infra-signal bus, adding egress_backpressure flag now.

maya: small note on metrics we should monitor during rollout: proxy_eject_rate, kvcache_eviction_rate, dedicated_spill_ratio, per-tenant session duration, p50/p95/p99 token latency, retry_count.

tasha: added whitelist for tenants: high-slo-team, payments-prod, internal-prod.

raj: canary done at 10% — preliminary: proxy_eject_rate down ~18% in canary cohort, p99 down 12% for that subset. Posting sample curl to exercise stream in canary: 

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"stream":true, "prompt":"short"}' https://hosted.eu-west.api/redwood/v1/generate
```
oncall: Good numbers. Ramp to 50% after +5m check.

infra-bot: +5m check: canary cohort metrics stable. kvcache_eviction_rate down 35% in canary. dedicated_spill_ratio unchanged globally yet — need scheduler hold to take effect.

luca: scheduler hold is live. Preventing scheduled spillovers triggered by proxy_eject heuristics for 1h.

maya: Great. Costs: oncall provided rough delta — estimated 18% token overhead saved by reduced retries, but dedicated min-reserve will add a 6% infra overhead for next 1h. Net win.

tasha: will keep min-reserve + whitelist for 1h, then revert and do a postmortem if stable.

maya: After we stabilize, follow-ups: 1) longer-term: mirror a lightweight backpressure signal from proxy to scheduler (persistent), 2) revisit KV cache sharding to be more tenant-aware, 3) consider small-embedding batching gate to reduce fanout.

raj: Agree. Also propose a 'streaming token pool' limiter per-tenant to protect KV shards.

maya: OK team — thanks. We'll keep this thread updated with telemetry and the postmortem plan. :thumbsup:
